steps.title: Game rules
steps.body: Logic makes a map a game: when something happens (an event), do something (actions). Here it decides what the chest holds: when the cinematic sends “scene-opens-chest”, logic opens the lid, puts the item in the chest, lifts it out and gives it to the hero. Graph and code are two views of the same rules. Every field has a “?”: hover it (or click it) to see what the field is and where its value comes from.

steps.title: A graph for the chest
steps.body: A graph holds rules: event chains that start with an event node (teal). + New makes one that starts with “On start”. Name graphs after what they are about, so you find them later.
steps.task: Make a new graph named “Treasure chest”.

how.text: In the panel on the left, next to “Graphs”, click “+ New”. A graph “Logic …” opens with an “On start” node.
At the top of the editor, click the graph’s name, select it, type Treasure chest and press Enter.

do.say: Type Treasure chest as the graph’s name and press Enter.

steps.title: The chest’s item is a variable
steps.body: Variables remember things while playing. A variable has three parts, each labelled in the form: a Name you invent (here chestItem: nothing else is called that, it is just our label), a Type (Text, because it holds a name) and a Starting value: Sword, the name of the built-in Sword asset as the Assets screen lists it. The rules read chestItem instead of saying “Sword”, so changing this one value makes the chest give any asset. Each variable card lists where it is used.
steps.task: Add a variable: Name chestItem, Type Text, Starting value Sword.

how.text: Under “Variables” (left), in the box “New variable”: in “Name” type chestItem; in “Type” pick “Text”; in “Starting value” type Sword (spelled as the asset’s name in the Assets screen); then click “Add variable”. A card “chestItem” appears: Type Text, Starting value Sword.

do.say: Type chestItem in “Name”: a name we invent.
Pick “Text” in “Type”: it holds a name.
Type Sword in “Starting value”: the Sword asset’s name.

steps.title: Listen for the cinematic
steps.body: Events start a chain. “On custom event” runs when something sends exactly its name: a cinematic, an asset interaction, another graph. “scene-opens-chest” is a name we invent here; the scene you direct in Cinematics will send it at the moment Rowan lifts the lid. (The chest asset has its own event, “chest-opened”, sent when a player presses E at it: a different name, not used in this story.)
steps.task: Add an “On custom event” node for the event “scene-opens-chest”.

how.text: Under “Nodes” (left), type custom in “Find a node”, then click “On custom event”. The node appears in the graph and is selected: its settings show on the right.

do.say: Click “On custom event”: it is added and selected.

how.text: On the right, open “Event name”; the list shows the names your project already uses and who sends them. Pick “＋ New event…”, type scene-opens-chest and press Enter. The note under it says nothing sends it yet: the scene will, in Cinematics.

do.say: Open “Event name” and pick “＋ New event…”.

steps.title: Open the lid
steps.body: “Set state” switches a placed object to one of its states. “target” lists the objects placed on your maps by their asset’s name: “Treasure chest” is the built-in asset’s name (Assets screen), and we put one on your start map for this story; in Play the copy nearest the hero is used. “state” lists that asset’s states, as Assets › Treasure chest › States defines them: closed and open. The lid is a moving part that swings open over 0.7 s. Wires carry the flow from a white “then” pin to a white “in” pin.
steps.task: Add “Set state” (target Treasure chest, state open) and wire “On custom event” then → its in.

how.text: Type set state in “Find a node” (left) and click “Set state”. It is added and selected.

do.say: Type set state in “Find a node”.

how.text: On the right under “Values”, open “target” and pick “Treasure chest — placed on …” (the objects on your maps, by asset name).
Open “state” and pick “open” (the list now holds the Treasure chest’s states: closed and open). The note under it names where they come from.

do.say: Pick “open” in “state”: one of the chest’s states.

how.text: In the graph, drag from the white “then” pin of “On custom event” to the white “in” pin of “Set state”. A wire joins them: when the event comes, the lid opens.

do.say: Drag from “then” on “On custom event” to “in” on “Set state”.

steps.title: The rest as code
steps.body: The same rules as code: each node is a line. Spawn item at object puts the item named in chestItem inside the chest; Set state “out” makes it rise (the Sword’s moving part); Give item puts it in the hero’s bag. A second event, “scene-takes-sword” (another name we invent, sent by the scene), removes the floating sword when Rowan takes it. In code, "Treasure chest", "open" and "out" are the same names the pickers list: the asset’s name and its states (the Sword’s states are in and out). Split shows code and graph.
steps.task: Switch to Split and type the code; the graph grows with every line.

how.text: At the top of the editor, click “Split”: code on one side, the graph on the other.
In the code, below what is there, type the lines shown in the card (or select all the code and type them in its place). After a short pause the graph shows the new nodes and wires.

do.say: The code is typed; the graph follows.
